sections.hypothesis: In the regime model's volatile state, holding BTC or ETH after the MACD 12/26/9 histogram is positive beats holding the same coin at the same average exposure, after costs.
sections.rationale: The volatile-spell direction study (note which-way-do-volatile-spells-go-macd, 2026-11-14) found TREND: on volatile days the week after a positive MACD histogram returned +1.63% and after a negative one -2.00% (BTC and ETH, 2021-05 to 2025-10, 75 non-overlapping weeks, P 98%). Economic reason: volatile spells are when new information arrives and is absorbed over days, not at once, so moves started in them continue; trend-vol-target, the strategy on pursue, holds little in them (13% vs 54%), so this is the part it leaves. Outside evidence is mixed: Daniel and Moskowitz find the opposite (rebounds) in cross-sectional momentum's panic states; this study's own result is the reason to test it. Caveats fixed now: this backtest uses the same 2021-25 data as the study, so it checks costs, turnover and drawdowns rather than giving independent evidence; the study's 75 weeks overlap across two correlated coins, so its confidence was overstated; the real tests are the holdout year (weaker for an idea formed after it was used, since it was a bear market) and paper trading. Luke chose the designs (2026-11-14): a week's hold at full size, and the daily switch.
sections.rules: Implementation volatile-macd, 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml, BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1d, 2021-05 to 2025-10 (regime states exist from 2021-05). Four backtests: hold_days 7 (the main design, matching the study) and hold_days 1 (the daily switch) on each coin, each run as kestrel backtest SYMBOL --strategy volatile-macd --research <this note> --interval 1d --start 2021-05 --end 2025-10 --cash 330 --param hold_days=N. Then, for the scorecard, on each coin with hold_days 7: kestrel walk-forward (fixed rule, no grid, 24-month training and 6-month test windows) and kestrel robustness (hold_days moved to 0.5, 0.75, 1.25 and 1.5 times 7).
sections.falsification: Graded on the scorecard, per coin, for hold_days 7. It earns a recommendation of pursue on a coin only if it passes every applicable test except luck (deflated Sharpe), as the strategies already watched did; luck is expected to fail on this much data. The daily switch is preferred to the weekly hold only if, on both coins, it has the higher Sharpe and fails no scorecard test the weekly passes; otherwise it is a recorded comparison. Anything failing an applicable test besides luck: Claude recommends drop and Luke decides. Run once.
sections.parameters: hold_days 7 (main) and 1 (comparison); MACD 12/26/9 (textbook, untuned); the regime preset fixed in kestrel.regimes (3 states, volatile = the most volatile).
sections.costs: About 22 bps a round trip on BTC, 23 on ETH. The daily switch trades far more and must earn its fees. Four backtests (four trials) plus the walk-forward and robustness looks, all counted.
